Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) or 'n.d.'; partial dates use YYYY or YYYY-MM. verification_status is 'opened' (the page was read during research) or 'listed' (found in a directory or link list, not read). case.name: City of Paris Open Source Program Office
case.local_name: OSPO de la Ville de Paris (Direction des Systèmes d'Information et du Numérique)

authorizing_act.title: None found. Self-reported creation date 2022-06-01 (FLOSS-PSO directory); the office was 'being defined' in July 2023.

case.placement: Project officer inside the city's IT department (DSIN), software engineering bureau, working alongside the Lutece engineering team

headcount.note: One named open source program officer. The 15-person figure is the Lutece engineering team, with 60-plus contractors; not the OSPO.

budget.note: No OSPO budget published. Lutece funding 'stems exclusively from the city budget' (OSOR 2020).

case.role_in_procurement_detail: No source describes a procurement review, an options analysis for proprietary purchases, or an exceptions register. The office's remit is the Lutece platform, its community, CiteLibre packaging and support to other authorities. Paris studied and shelved a desktop migration in 2003-04 and signed a Microsoft partnership in 2008.
functions: CiteLibre: packaging Lutece into deployable packs for other authorities
community events, webinars and contributor guides for the Lutece community
support for local authorities that want to deploy Lutece
faster handling of internal pull requests; review committee for outside contributions
inventory of open source components and their dependencies
memberships: April (2015), EU OSPO Network co-founder (2022), OW2, OSPO++, OSPO Alliance (2024)

key_people.name: Philippe Bareille
key_people.role: Open Source Program Officer, City of Paris CIO office; co-maintainer of the FLOSS-PSO registry

key_people.name: Magali Lemaire
key_people.role: Head of the software engineering bureau (apparent manager of the officer)

outcomes_reported.note: City claimed 300+ in 2021-22; use the current portal figure and date it.

outcomes_reported.metric: share of city servers on GNU/Linux

outcomes_reported.note: A hospital group and one municipality; about ten authorities interested.

stated_reasons_for_open_source: reuse of a city-owned platform for every new service instead of procuring again
mutualisation: software paid for once by Paris, maintained by a community, deployed by others at no license cost
permissive BSD licence chosen 'to make it easy to reuse and hack, not to protect our codebase'
support for other public bodies and cities (CiteLibre)

un_principles_mapping.open_by_default: 2002 council vote to publish Lutece; practice since, but no policy text and no exception mechanism
un_principles_mapping.contribute_back: memberships of April, OW2, OSPO Alliance; community contributions reviewed by a committee
un_principles_mapping.secure_by_design: component inventory with versions and dependencies maintained with OSPO support
un_principles_mapping.foster_inclusive_participation: Lutece community events, webinars, contributor guides; co-founded EU OSPO Network
un_principles_mapping.design_for_reusability: CiteLibre packs; BSD 3-Clause; deployments in Lyon, Marseille, Budapest, Accra, Baltimore
un_principles_mapping.provide_documentation: opensource.paris.fr and lutece.paris.fr; self-reported weakness in merging contributions
un_principles_mapping.rise: officer helps maintain the global FLOSS-PSO registry; support to adopting authorities
un_principles_mapping.sustain_and_scale: twenty years of one platform; no charter, no published budget or savings figure

lessons_for_nyc: Package every PIT Crew product the way CiteLibre packages Lutece: deployable by the next agency or city without the original team, under a license chosen for reuse.
Charter the office in legislation; Paris's office has no founding document, so its remit is whatever its officer and bureau decide.
Add the three jobs Paris's office was never given: required review of technology contracts above a threshold, ownership of the options analysis, a public register of exceptions.
Use the Paris officer and the FLOSS-PSO registry as the entry point to the European network; Paris and New York already sit together in the Cities Coalition for Digital Rights.

analysis_brief.title: Paris OSPO Brief
analysis_brief.note: The brief renders under the Paris case on /success (content/briefs/paris.md); this path is site-relative on purpose.

gaps: No founding deliberation, charter or strategy for the OSPO was found; ask opensource@paris.fr before describing it as 'created in 2022'.
OSPO headcount beyond the one officer is unverified; the 15-person figure is the Lutece engineering team.
Service counts conflict (300+, 200+, about 100, 80%); use '200-plus' with the city portal as source and date it.
Current Microsoft or other proprietary spend by the city was not found.
The 'more than 40 cities' figure is the EC's; the 'over 50 organisations' figure is from 2020; neither is from the city.
2003-04 migration study figures are from contemporaneous French press and a 2008 political document; confirm the 57.4% discount in a second source.
